name: Hungarian Secession ceramics
summary: Colourful architectural ceramics of the Hungarian Secession. Ödön Lechner and the Zsolnay factory made frost-proof pyrogranite tiles and iridescent eosin glazes for roofs, domes and facades.

philosophy.core_thesis: A national style needs a national material: frost-proof, bright clay tiles with Hungarian folk flowers and Eastern patterns make a roof into the face of a building.
design_principles: Cover the roof with glazed tiles in 3 or 4 colours, laid in zigzag and diamond patterns.
Mould the tiles from pyrogranite, a clay fired at a very high heat that resists frost.
Draw the ornament from Hungarian folk art: tulips, pomegranates, peacocks and stylised leaves.
Use the iridescent eosin glaze on the finials, the crown pieces and the wall panels.
Frame the arches and the gates with bands of relief and a ceramic mosaic.
Fire the tiles in a single, hot firing so that the colours do not fade.
Set a bright ridge, a finial and a tower top on the roof line.
anti_patterns: A plain grey roof of slate or metal
Gothic or classical ornament with no folk pattern
Thin, delicate porcelain in place of a hard tile
Fine details in a pale, even glaze

form.shape: Roof tiles, ridge pieces, finials, facade panels, window frames and moulded relief tiles for gates and towers.
form.profile: A roof of steep pitch; the tile is flat or scale-shaped and sits in rows; the finial rises in a tulip or a pointed form.
form.foot_and_rim: The tile has a nib at the back for the batten and a smooth, even edge; the finial has a socket for the ridge.
form.proportion: A roof tile is about 20 to 40 cm long and 12 to 15 mm thick; a finial stands 40 to 100 cm high.
rules: Use bright colour in a repeated pattern on the roof.
Make each tile hard and frost-proof.
Use folk flowers and Eastern shapes for the relief.
Give the ridge a bright piece of eosin lustre.

bodies.rule: Use a hard pyrogranite body for tile and relief, and a finer faience body for the small ornamental pieces. Both must resist frost.

forming.joins: Roof tiles hang on battens with a nib; panels are set in mortar on a backing wall, and the finial is fixed on the ridge with an iron pin.
forming.details: A bright, uneven glaze at the edge, a stamp of the factory on the back and a fine web of crackle on some pieces.

glaze.pattern: Tulips, peacocks and folk flowers in relief; zigzag and diamond roof patterns in green, yellow, orange and blue; eosin lustre in red, purple and gold.
glaze.gloss: Gloss, about 70 to 95 GU; the eosin glaze has an oily metallic sheen that shifts with the light.
glaze.wear: The frost-proof tile keeps its colour for more than a century; the eosin lustre can lose a little shine, and an edge may chip.

palette.strategy: Strong colours on a roof: green, orange-yellow, cobalt and a deep red, with the eosin lustre in purple and gold as the final accent.

firing.kiln: A large coal-fired kiln of a ceramics factory; the tile stands in stacks, and a high firing brings the body to a hard, dense state.
processes: pressing and drying of the body
a reduction pass for the eosin lustre
firing.scale: A factory of several hundred workers in Pécs, which supplied roofs and facades across Hungary and the Austro-Hungarian empire.
firing.signs: A factory stamp on the back, strong colour and gloss on the roof tile, and a lustre that changes colour from one angle to the next.

pieces.form: Scale-shaped glazed roof tile in green and orange for a zigzag roof
Tulip finial in eosin glaze for a ridge or a tower top
Facade panel with a peacock and flowers in pyrogranite relief
Faience panel with a folk flower in blue and green on cream
Ridge crest with stylised leaves in blue and green glaze

positive: glazed zigzag roof tiles in green and orange
frost-proof tile with a hard gloss

emotion.target_response: Joy and national pride: the viewer sees a bright roof that glows with colour and folk art.

use_cases: a render of a Budapest building with a ceramic roof
a conservation note on pyrogranite tiles
a roof or finial design in folk colours
avoid_when: the brief needs a muted, earth-coloured roof
the brief needs a minimal, flat facade
the brief needs a Western Gothic roof

modifiers.how: Break the tile into shards and set them in mortar on a curved surface in free colour.
Remove the lustre, use buff and red clay and set the ornament in deep relief.

ornament_level.note: Roof colour and eosin lustre carry the style; ornament stays high.

wall_thickness.note: Roof tiles are thin; relief panels reach 25 mm.
